headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Replit Agent’s broad network/filesystem access can expose ms-swift artifacts and secrets when paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and Replit Agent persists workspace state across sessions. ms-swift consumes files and logs via CLI/Python workflows, so attacker-controlled content in shared files could be treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from overlapping file surfaces.
conditions: IF the pair shares a writable workspace or copied files
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted files
Add a manual review step before either agent reads shared artifacts
Use read-only mounts for handoff files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift handles hub tokens and SDK tokens, while Replit Agent handles Replit Secrets and third-party API keys. Replit Agent also has broad network egress and workspace persistence, so secrets or sensitive code in shared files can be exfiltrated or retained. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default cloud-workspace use.
conditions: IF either agent is given the same workspace containing secrets
IF Replit Agent uploads or transmits workspace contents to external services
IF ms-swift writes secrets into logs or training outputs
mitigations: Move secrets to separate vaults
Rotate any exposed tokens immediately
Restrict shared files to non-sensitive artifacts
Turn off persistence for handoff directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping and redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, install packages, read/write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Replit Agent additionally modifies git state and runs in a persistent Repl filesystem, so concurrent writes can collide and corrupt code or deployment state. ms-swift lacks stated locking or multi-instance coordination, making conflict likely if both touch the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory
IF either agent modifies git state or generated files without locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize write operations
Pause one agent during the other's edits
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file locks and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Replit Agent can act on workspace changes and deployment-related APIs, while ms-swift can generate outputs from files and logs. If Replit Agent consumes ms-swift output without verification, errors can cascade into code or deployment changes. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream actions by both agents.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses ms-swift output as authoritative input
IF ms-swift produces generated code, configs, or recommendations
IF downstream deployment actions are triggered from that output
mitigations: Require human review before acting on generated output
Add validation tests between agents
Limit ms-swift output to drafts only
Log and diff all handoffs
requires-engineering: implement schema-checked inter-agent contracts

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, evaluation outputs, and configuration data, while Replit Agent touches source code, secrets, and deployment configuration. The profiles do not state residency or certification mismatches, but the mixed data classes and Replit’s cloud-hosted workspace create a plausible retention and handling mismatch. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either workspace
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two environments
IF secrets or customer data are stored in Replit-managed storage
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document retention settings for each workspace
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
Use synthetic data for testing
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
